sections.h2: Lincoln as a place to sell
sections.html:
Nebraska's capital is also Lancaster County's seat and the state's second-largest city. It covers about 104 square miles, so the age, lot size and condition of a house vary a great deal from one part of town to another. The combined area with Beatrice has about 372,000 residents by a 2024 estimate.

State government, Lincoln Public Schools and the University of Nebraska-Lincoln are the largest employers, with Bryan Health and St. Elizabeth Regional Medical Center adding shift workers. Sellers who relocate, inherit a house or divorce are among those who may want a faster closing than a listing offers.

Lincoln mixes old and new neighborhoods, and the age of a house usually decides what an inspector will flag. Several areas started as their own towns before the city annexed them: Bethany in 1922, University Place in 1926, College View in 1929, Havelock in 1930 and West Lincoln in 1966. Historic districts sit near downtown, while newer subdivisions have spread mostly south and east.

  • Former towns such as Havelock, College View and University Place: expect questions about older wiring, plumbing and foundations on small lots.
  • Historic districts near downtown: deferred exterior upkeep and rental conversions come up.
  • South and east subdivisions: systems are newer, but the disclosure form still applies.

sections.h2: Weather and the roof, furnace and foundation
sections.html:
Lincoln has cold winters, hot humid summers and thunderstorms that sometimes produce tornadoes. Snow averages 26 inches a season. The city averages 41.8 days at 90 degrees or hotter and 10.1 nights at 0 degrees or lower.

Those swings are hard on shingles, gutters, concrete steps and older furnaces, and a buyer's inspector will look at all of them. If yours are tired, a cash sale lets you skip the repair list and sell the house in its current state.

sections.h2: Certificate of Compliance for rental buildings
sections.html:
The biggest Lincoln-specific rule applies to buildings with three or more rental units, not to a typical single-family home. The owner of a property with three or more residential units must give a prospective buyer, at transfer, either a valid Certificate of Compliance or a notice of Minimum Housing Code deficiencies from the Building Official.

Certificate itemAmount
First three units$90
Each additional unit$12
Fire inspection fee$70
  • A certificate is valid for 90 days from issuance.
  • Inspectors check items such as roof structure, handrails, gutters, windows, smoke detectors and electrical safety.
  • If a buyer closes without a certificate, getting one becomes the buyer's job, and code deficiencies stay with the current owner.

A Neglected Building Registry covers vacant and neglected buildings. Since June 2021, a short-term rental license costs $250 per unit and renews every year, with a cap of 10 percent of units in multi-family premises in the R-1 through R-8 districts. If you run a listing on a house you plan to sell, check the license status first. The buyer will need to sort out their own license with the city's Planning and Development Services.

sections.h2: Nebraska disclosure rules for Lincoln sellers
sections.html:
Selling a home with one to four dwelling units means handing the buyer a signed written disclosure statement. Timing matters: it must be delivered on or before the effective date of any binding purchase contract. Nebraska Revised Statute 76-2,120 is the rule, and it lets you write "unknown" for anything outside your personal knowledge.

Topics on the form include appliances, electrical, heating and cooling, water and sewer systems, hazardous conditions, title issues such as easements, and carbon monoxide alarm compliance. A buyer who never receives the form can sue for actual damages, court costs and attorney's fees.

The statute carves out some transfers. A fiduciary administering a decedent's estate is excluded unless that person lived in the home. Foreclosure sales and transfers between spouses or to lineal relatives are excluded too.

sections.h2: Deeds and property taxes in Lancaster County
sections.html:
The Lancaster County Assessor/Register of Deeds Office records the deed, and the County Treasurer bills and collects property tax. When a deed is recorded, Nebraska charges a documentary stamp tax on the seller. From July 18, 2026, the rate is $3.32 for each $1,000 of value or fraction of $1,000, up from $2.32. A Real Estate Transfer Statement (Form 521) must be signed for the deed to be recorded.

Property tax is due each year on December 31. State law allows two half payments without interest before the delinquent dates of April 1 and August 1. The bill funds schools, the county, the city, fire districts and other local bodies, so it shows several levies.

At closing, the title company normally splits the current year's tax between you and the buyer. Ask for the parcel number early so you can check what has been billed.

The right choice depends on the condition of the house, how long you can wait and what you owe. A traditional listing may bring a higher price but adds showings, an inspection, repair requests and a financing contingency. A cash sale to a company like ours removes most of that, usually at a lower price.

  • Pick a listing if the house is in good shape and you can wait through a few months of showings.
  • Consider a cash sale if you inherited a house you do not want to repair, if tenants are in place, or if a move date is close.
  • Compare any offer against what a repaired and listed house would net after commissions, repairs and carrying costs.

sections.h2: Selling a Lincoln house, step by step
sections.html:
The order below applies to a listing and to a direct cash sale alike.

  1. Get the parcel number from the Lancaster County Assessor/Register of Deeds records so you know what the county has on file.
  2. Fill out the disclosure form before you accept any offer.
  3. If the building has three or more units, order the Certificate of Compliance or the deficiency notice from the Building Official.
  4. Sign the purchase contract and deliver the disclosure by the effective date.
  5. Sign the Real Estate Transfer Statement (Form 521) with the deed.
  6. The title company prorates property tax, pays off liens and files the deed for recording. The documentary stamp tax comes out of your side.

Many Lincoln sellers are estates. The statute excludes a fiduciary's transfer from the disclosure form unless the fiduciary lived there, which can shorten the paperwork. You still need authority to sell, a clear deed chain and a payoff on any tax or lien. Ask the title company early what documents it wants from the estate so closing day is not delayed.

If the house is vacant, check whether it falls under the Neglected Building Registry, and keep the roof, gutters and entry points in decent shape while you decide how to sell.

faqs.q: Do I need a Certificate of Compliance to sell my house in Lincoln?
faqs.a: Only if the property has three or more residential units. Owners of those buildings must give the buyer a valid certificate or a deficiency notice at transfer. A single-family house does not need one.

faqs.q: How much is the Nebraska deed tax on a Lincoln home sale?
faqs.a: The documentary stamp tax is $3.32 per $1,000 of value for deeds recorded on or after July 18, 2026. The seller owes it, and the Lancaster County Register of Deeds collects it when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: When are Lancaster County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due December 31 each year. April 1 and August 1 are the delinquent dates for the two half payments.

faqs.q: Do I have to give a disclosure statement if I sell for cash?
faqs.a: Yes, for a one-to-four unit home, unless a statutory exception applies. Nebraska law covers residential sellers whether the buyer pays cash or uses a loan. Estate fiduciaries who never lived in the home are one exception.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lincoln house that has a short-term rental license?
faqs.a: You can sell it. The license is issued per rental unit and renewed annually at $250, so the buyer will need to sort out their own license with the city.
